strengths: Original and timely conceptual framework: Redesigning flow maps to inherently support test-time reward alignment via stochasticity bridges the gap between fast distilled generators and principled inference-time guidance/SMC.

Strong theoretical contributions: Proposition 4.3 elegantly reveals that the DDPM transition kernel is directly embedded in the Posterior Diamond Map via early stopping in inner time $s$, bypassing the need for separate transition network distillation or noisy round-trips.

Comprehensive two-pronged formulation: The paper provides both Posterior Diamond Maps (distilled directly from GLASS flows for exact posterior sampling) and Weighted Diamond Maps (enabling off-the-shelf deterministic flow maps to act as consistent value estimators via renoising and importance weighting).

Thorough empirical evaluation across domains and scales: Validates the methods across image super-resolution, class-to-text steerability, and high-resolution text-to-image benchmarks (GenEval, UniGenBench++) on competitive modern models (FLUX.1-dev and SANA-Sprint 0.6B), clearly mapping out NFE-vs-quality Pareto frontiers against competitive baselines (Best-of-N, DPS, and Flow Map Guidance).
weaknesses: Gap between theory and practice for Weighted Diamond Maps: In Section 5 and Appendix D.2.1, the authors note that the theoretically consistent weights derived in Proposition 5.1 break down in high dimensions because score and likelihood gradients dominate the reward gradient. Consequently, the practical implementation discards the theoretical weighting, simplifies $w_k$ to reward-only softmax, and heuristically unit-normalizes each gradient component before summing. While practically effective, this undermines the central theoretical claim of using a mathematically consistent value gradient estimator in the high-resolution experiments.

Additional training overhead for Posterior Diamond Maps: While Weighted Diamond Maps can use existing checkpoints, Posterior Diamond Maps require distilling GLASS flows with extra conditioning variables $(x_t, t)$ and time parameters $(s, s')$. This increases model parameter count/architecture modifications and limits immediate plug-and-play adoption for existing foundation models.

Minor presentation polish issues: Several minor typographical and formatting issues exist, including an incomplete repository link in Appendix D ('Code for our experiments can be found under .'), dangling citations in Section C ('Liu et al.; Domingo-Enrich et al., 2024'), and minor typos such as 'closer to th problem' on page 11.

strengths: Principled and novel formulation: The paper tackles a core bottleneck in diffusion/flow reward alignment—the bias of the standard denoiser approximation for the value function—by introducing stochastic flow maps that amortize posterior sampling and transition steps into single evaluations.

Comprehensive theoretical framework with two versatile variants: (1) Posterior Diamond Maps, which distill GLASS flows to directly sample posteriors and elegantly yield time-reversal DDPM transitions via early stopping (Proposition 4.3) without explicit retraining; and (2) Weighted Diamond Maps, which enable consistent value-function gradient estimation on top of off-the-shelf deterministic flow maps via renoising and importance correction (Proposition 5.1).

Thorough empirical verification across tasks and architectures: Evaluated on unconditional/class-conditional generation, linear inverse problems (super-resolution on CelebA and ImageNet), SMC, and modern large-scale text-to-image models (SANA-Sprint 0.6B and FLUX.1-dev flow map) using standard disentangled benchmarks (GenEval and UniGenBench++).

Favorable compute scaling: Convincingly demonstrates that scaling Monte Carlo look-ahead samples achieves a steeper Pareto frontier against NFE than traditional Best-of-N or increasing ODE solver steps.
weaknesses: Gap between theory and practical implementation for Weighted Diamond Maps: While Proposition 5.1 rigorously derives consistent importance weights and score corrections, Section 7.2 and Appendix D.2.1 note that at high dimensions, the analytical weights are discarded and replaced with a heuristic unit-normalization of each gradient component due to dimensionality scaling issues. The paper should more prominently acknowledge and discuss the implications of this practical heuristic relative to the theoretical consistency guarantee.

Architectural complexity and distillation overhead for Posterior Diamond Maps: Posterior Diamond Maps require parameterizing and conditioning networks on four time arguments $(t, t', s, s')$ and two image representations $(x_t,  ar{x}_s)$, which adds noticeable training overhead (e.g., 800k steps on 6x A100 for CelebA-64) compared to standard flow matching models.

Latency and compute cost in practical settings: In Table 1, Weighted Diamond Maps with FLUX requires 483 seconds per generation compared to 46 seconds for Flow Map Guidance. Backpropagating through both the reward model and the flow map substantially increases memory and wall-clock time, which merits deeper discussion alongside the NFE comparisons.

Presentation polish and minor omissions: There is a placeholder link left empty on page 25 ('Code for our experiments can be found under .'), inconsistent references between 'Theorem' and 'Proposition' (e.g., Proposition 4.3 referred to as Theorem 4.3 in Section 7.1), and minor typographical/grammatical slips (e.g., page 10: 'in this different model classwhile mc scaling seems less powerful Section D.1.').

strengths: The paper addresses a central and challenging problem in generative modeling: performing fast, principled inference-time reward alignment without incurring the heavy computational cost of full ODE/SDE rollouts or relying on oversimplified point-mass posterior approximations.

The theoretical insight in Proposition 4.3 ('Diamond DDPM sampling') is elegant: it demonstrates that stopping the inner flow of a distilled GLASS model early and mapping back via the sufficient statistic yields exact transitions from the DDPM time-reversal SDE, effectively providing one-step transition proposals for SMC/search without dedicated retraining.

The proposed framework offers two complementary angles: Posterior Diamond Maps (amortizing GLASS flows into a fast posterior sampler) and Weighted Diamond Maps (a training-free adaptation for existing off-the-shelf deterministic flow maps via renoising and importance weighting).

Strong and extensive empirical evaluation on modern, large-scale text-to-image models (FLUX.1-dev flowmap and SANA-Sprint 0.6B) across standardized alignment benchmarks (GenEval and UniGenBench++), demonstrating clear compute-scaling advantages over Best-of-N and Flow Map Guidance baselines.
weaknesses: Divergence between theory and practical execution in Weighted Diamond Maps: Proposition 5.1 carefully derives a consistent estimator featuring composite weights and score/likelihood corrections. However, Section 7.2 and Section D.2.1 reveal that due to dimensionality mismatch in practice, the theoretical weights are discarded entirely, replaced with reward-only softmax weights, and individual gradient components are ad-hoc unit-normalized before scaling with a heuristic hyperparameter $\lambda$. This weakens the connection between the formal theoretical claims and the empirical algorithm.

Performance trade-off in unconditional sample quality for Posterior Diamond Maps: As shown in Table 3, Posterior Diamond Maps exhibit non-trivial FID degradation compared to standard flow maps across benchmarks (e.g., CIFAR-10 FID 12.55 vs. 10.60; CelebA-64 FID 16.08 vs. 9.53; ImageNet-1k FID 10.74 vs. 6.06 for 1-step). The additional conditioning on $(t, t', s, s')$ and $\bar{x}_s$ appears to introduce significant learning difficulty.

Notational and referencing inconsistencies throughout the manuscript: Several formal statements are inconsistently labeled between the main text and appendix (e.g., Proposition 4.1 vs. Theorem 4.1 in Section A.3; Proposition 4.3 vs. Theorem 4.3 in Section 4.2; Proposition 5.1 vs. Theorem 5.1 in Section 5 and Figure 3). Additionally, minor indexing errors appear in Algorithm 1 (e.g., line 6 assigning to $z^i$ while using index $k$).

strengths: Sound theoretical framework: The paper provides a principled formulation connecting stochastic flow maps, posterior sampling (via GLASS Flows), and consistent value function estimation for reward alignment, moving beyond standard biased denoiser approximations (e.g., the Jensen gap).

Novel dual-design approach: The paper proposes two complementary solutions tailored to different practical trade-offs: (1) Posterior Diamond Maps, which distill the full posterior sampling process into a one-step model, and (2) Weighted Diamond Maps, an inference-time plug-in method that equips off-the-shelf deterministic flow maps with consistent importance-weighted value gradient estimates.

Insightful connection to DDPM transitions (Proposition 4.3): Demonstrating that the time-reversal SDE transition kernel is implicitly embedded in an early-stopped Posterior Diamond Map via sufficient statistics is an elegant and practically useful finding for multi-step search and SMC.

Solid empirical results on high-resolution text-to-image synthesis: Evaluating Weighted Diamond Maps on SANA-Sprint 0.6B at 1024x1024 resolution on the GenEval benchmark demonstrates convincing quantitative improvements (0.83 vs. 0.70 baseline, outperforming Best-of-N and ReNO) while maintaining computational efficiency.

Clear presentation and intuitive visualizations: Figures 1, 2, and 3 clearly illustrate the conceptual differences between naive re-noising, deterministic flow map extrapolation, and the proposed stochastic flow map corrections.
weaknesses: Scale disparity between the two proposed methods: Due to the need to train specialized architectures conditioned on both inner and outer time variables, Posterior Diamond Maps are only evaluated on small toy benchmarks (CIFAR-10, CelebA-64), whereas the large-scale T2I experiments rely solely on Weighted Diamond Maps.

Approximation error in line-integral quadrature: Proposition 5.1 states consistency, but the practical estimator relies on a trapezoidal quadrature approximation for the line integral term $\gamma_i$. The impact of this approximation as $|t' - t|$ increases is not theoretically bounded or thoroughly ablated.

Saturation with respect to particle count: Table 4 indicates that performance plateaus quickly for $K \ge 4$ particles. While this keeps inference fast, it suggests that the effective sample size (ESS) in high-dimensional spaces might degrade the benefits of additional Monte Carlo sampling.

Minor indexing and notation inconsistencies: There are minor typographical inaccuracies in algorithm boxes (e.g., in Algorithm 1, line 6 defines $z^i$ while line 7 uses $z^k$; in Algorithm 3 line 21, $\delta_{\text{score}}^i$ is used inside a sum indexed by $k$).

strengths: Principled and novel formulation: The paper tackles a key bottleneck in inference-time reward alignment—the intractability or bias of value function estimation—by cleverly designing stochastic flow maps.

Theoretical elegance of Proposition 4.3 (Diamond DDPM Sampling): Demonstrating that one-step time-reversal SDE / DDPM transitions are analytically embedded via early stopping in the GLASS flow parameterization is a notable theoretical contribution that avoids costly or error-accumulating denoise-then-renoise loops.

Practicality of Weighted Diamond Maps (Proposition 5.1): Developing a mathematically consistent, score-corrected importance sampling estimator that works directly with existing off-the-shelf distilled flow maps (without retraining) offers immediate practical utility.

Strong empirical performance on modern benchmarks: On SANA-Sprint (1024x1024 text-to-image), Weighted Diamond Maps achieve state-of-the-art alignment results on GenEval (0.83 mean score), outperforming ReNO and Best-of-N with superior inference time and scaling curves.
Thorough derivations and proofs: Appendices A.1 through A.10 provide clear, complete mathematical derivations for the GLASS reparameterizations, value function gradients, and score corrections.
weaknesses: Evaluation scope for Posterior Diamond Maps is limited: Posterior Diamond Maps are only evaluated on low-resolution benchmarks (CIFAR-10 and CelebA-64). While authors cite compute constraints, evaluating whether distilled posterior flow maps scale gracefully to modern text-to-image or higher-resolution architectures remains an open question.

Quality trade-off in Posterior Diamond Maps: Table 3 reveals that Posterior Diamond Maps suffer a noticeable degradation in baseline generation quality compared to standard deterministic flow maps (e.g., 1-step FID worsens from 9.53 to 16.08 on CelebA-64, and from 10.60 to 12.55 on CIFAR-10), indicating that conditioning on four time/state variables simultaneously increases model difficulty.

Memory and backpropagation overhead: Computing $\nabla_{x_t} r(X_{0,1}(\bar{x}_0 | x_t, t))$ or the corresponding term in Weighted Diamond Maps requires backpropagating through both the reward model and the flow map network. The manuscript lacks a discussion or reporting of peak VRAM footprint and memory scaling across particle count $K$.

Approximations in Weighted Diamond Maps: The consistency of Weighted Diamond Maps relies on an exact path integral $\gamma_i$, which in practice is approximated via single-step trapezoidal quadrature. A brief empirical or numerical error analysis of this quadrature approximation would strengthen the validity of the practical algorithm.

strengths: Principled and well-motivated framework: The paper addresses a fundamental bottleneck in inference-time reward guidance—intractable and biased value function estimation via the denoiser—by constructing stochastic flow maps.

Strong theoretical contributions: The formulation of Posterior Diamond Maps (distilling GLASS flows) and Proposition 4.3 (showing that early-stopped Diamond maps yield exact DDPM transitions) are theoretically elegant. Proposition 5.1 provides an actionable, consistent estimator for existing pre-trained flow maps with exact score corrections.
Practical versatility: Weighted Diamond Maps require no re-training and act as an off-the-shelf inference-time guidance technique for existing distilled flow models.

Convincing empirical validation: Evaluated on high-resolution text-to-image synthesis (1024x1024 SANA-Sprint 0.6B), Weighted Diamond Maps clearly outperform competitive inference-time alignment baselines (Best-of-N, ReNO, Prompt Optimization) on GenEval while being significantly more compute- and time-efficient.
weaknesses: Scale limitations for Posterior Diamond Maps: While Weighted Diamond Maps are demonstrated at scale, Posterior Diamond Maps are only evaluated on toy/small-scale datasets (CIFAR-10, CelebA-64) because training requires distilling GLASS flows with additional time and conditioning variables. It remains unclear how easily this scales to multi-billion parameter text-to-image foundations.

Quadrature accuracy under large step sizes: For Weighted Diamond Maps, the path integral $\gamma_i$ is approximated via single-step trapezoidal quadrature. However, the best results in Table 4 are obtained at a relatively large step size / SNR ratio ($\lambda = 20$). A discussion or empirical check on the bias/error introduced by this quadrature approximation under larger $\lambda$ is missing.

Minor indexing and notation inconsistencies in algorithms: In Algorithm 1, line 6 writes $z^i \leftarrow X_{0,1}^\theta(\bar{x}_0^k | x_t, t)$ while line 7 uses $z^k$; in Algorithm 3, line 17 defines $\delta_{\text{score}}^i$ instead of $\delta_{\text{score}}^k$, and line 21 mixes indices $i$ and $k$. These should be cleaned up.
Lack of variance/error bounds in empirical tables: Tables 1, 4, and 5 do not report standard deviations or confidence intervals across multiple evaluation runs or seeds.
